extract:
ROSALÍA is a Spanish singer, songwriter and producer born Rosalía Vila Tobella in 1992 in Sant Esteve Sesrovires, a town outside Barcelona in Catalonia. Active since the early 2010s, she emerged from Barcelona's flamenco world before becoming one of the most recognizable figures in global Latin pop, moving fluidly between flamenco, reggaeton, R&B and experimental electronic music.

Her formative years were shaped by a teenage obsession with flamenco, sparked in part by hearing Camarón de la Isla. She studied flamenco at the Escola Superior de Música de Catalunya in Barcelona, training under the cantaor José Miguel Vizcaya, known as El Chiqui. During that period she sang at weddings, bars and tablaos and worked as a backing and collaborating vocalist in the Catalan scene, absorbing traditional cante while also listening widely to pop, hip-hop and R&B.

Her debut album, Los Ángeles (2017), was a spare collaboration with guitarist and producer Raül Refree that reinterpreted old flamenco songs centered on death and longing, earning her a Latin Grammy nomination for Best New Artist. That year she also released the single Aunque Es De Noche. The breakthrough came with El Mal Querer (2018), a conceptual album co-produced with El Guincho (Pablo Díaz-Reixa) and structured in chapters inspired by the 13th-century Occitan novel Flamenca, tracing a toxic relationship. Singles such as MALAMENTE (Cap.1: Augurio) and PIENSO EN TU MIRÁ (Cap.3: Celos) fused palmas and flamenco melisma with trap beats, samples and pop production, and the album started as her master's project at the conservatory.

After signing with Sony Music, ROSALÍA pivoted toward urbano and pop. Con Altura (2019), with J Balvin and featuring El Guincho, became a global hit, and the Fucking Money Man release (Milionària and Dio$ No$ Libre Del Dinero) included a song in Catalan. The 2019 EP Yo x Ti, Tu x Mi with Ozuna, Aute Cuture and A Palé continued this streak, followed by Juro Que, Dolerme, TKN with Travis Scott, a remix of The Weeknd's Blinding Lights, and Lo Vas A Olvidar with Billie Eilish for the series Euphoria.

Critical reception has been strong. El Mal Querer won the Latin Grammy for Album of the Year in 2019, and ROSALÍA won a Grammy for Best Latin Rock, Urban or Alternative Album. She became a fixture of fashion and art-world culture as well as the charts. Her success also drew debate within Spain about cultural appropriation, since she is a non-Romani Catalan artist working with a tradition rooted in Romani communities.

She followed this period with MOTOMAMI (2022), a fragmented, maximalist record blending reggaeton, bachata, flamenco and industrial textures, which won the Latin Grammy for Album of the Year and confirmed her as an artist willing to reinvent herself with each project. Her legacy is that of an artist who took flamenco from conservatory study and Barcelona stages to the center of global pop, opening space for Spanish artists in the Latin urban mainstream.
title: ROSALÍA
